doc.title: Al Grey interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995

title: The Basie band's kangaroo court and the Bat Fund
summary: The band's secret mock court fines members; Grey is fined $10 for bringing two elderly women to meet Basie in Miami.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Which I cannot give completely in details, because that’s just like one of the, still, of the secrets of the Basie organization. And they had a thing in this where you could be brought up on charges, you could be brought up on charges, and that meant that if you was held getting drunk that night or something or something that day you could be brought up on charges for, and it was where if you were guilty, you had to pay a fine. You had pay a $5 fine. Now this kitty grew so much that they had enough money in the funds to give out for the [inaudible]. Because Basie would be brought up on charges too, see? They call it the Bat Fund. And so that means that he’s off tonight and you’re in the street somewhere and you’re out with a lady that didn’t come up to what they used to classify, is she a bear or is she beautiful, or — and they would — and that’s the way it was. And then he could come up with it was kind of touchy, they don’t know whether it was quite enough or whether to go on the other side, like was she ugly or — and so another thing, you’ll never hear this because this was completely secret of that band. But I finally got out of the club. We were playing down at the Deauville Hotel on the beach in Miami, Florida and this night, it was two elderly ladies, one was in her seventies and the other lady was in her eighties. Now I brought these two ladies to meet Count Basie because they had been going to see Count Basie in their younger life. And this hotel was a hotel where they used to have a lot of people that retired and they stayed there. Now they wanted to come and say hello to Mr. Basie, and let him know that they loved his ©Fillius Jazz Archive -11-

music for many, many years. Well, this fund was a no-no. I had no business to be taking these elderly ladies, so they brought me up to court and I was charged $10, because now I had two, you see, and I’m charged $10 for these two elderly ladies, which I had no business being there, see, so as far as the kangaroo court was concerned. So this is when I resigned. Because I said to Basie, I said, “Chief you know, you know darn well that there’s nothing going on or anything here, they wanted to meet you and I brought them here.” And they said “well he brought them there where Count Basie could get the fine so we feel as though we should put the fine on you.” Because now Basie would say come in and relax and have a glass of water or something there. He would have been liable for that. See we had lawyers and all like this see in the kangaroo court. In fact I was one of the lawyers. And the judge is still with the Count Basie band today. Bill Hughes, he’s the judge. And Mario Bauza is still the Treasurer, who collects this money. So this is still, but they have indicated that if someone was sick that was in the band, they would take money out of this fund, because this was — and this was a lot of stuff. And the gentleman who we’re going to talk about a little later on, same difference, because he did one thing one time —
